Tuning coalescing parameters on NIC can be really hard.
Servers can handle both bulk and RPC like traffic
goals : bulk flows want as big GRO packets as possible
latencies.
To reach big GRO packets on 10Gbe NIC
ethtool -C eth0 rx-usecs 4 rx-frames 44
But this penalizes rpc sessions
50% in some cases
column2: as NICs generally do not force an interrupt when

column1: a packet with TCP Push flag is received.
Some NICs do not have an absolute timer
column2: only a timer rearmed for every

column1: incoming packet.
This patch uses a different strategy : Let GRO stack decides what do do
based on traffic pattern.
Packets with Push flag wont be delayed.
Packets without Push flag might be held in GRO engine
receiving data.
This new mechanism is off by default
column2: and shall be enabled by setting

column1: /sys/class/net/ethX/gro_flush_timeout to a value in nanosecond.
To fully enable this mechanism
instead of napi_complete().
Tested:
Ran 200 netperf TCP_STREAM from A to B (10Gbe mlx4 link
Without this feature
GRO aggregation ratio is low (811/305 = 2.65 segments per GRO packet)
Setting a timer of 2000 nsec is enough to increase GRO packet sizes
and reduce number of ACK packets. (811/19.2 = 42)
Receiver performs less calls to upper stacks
This also reduces cpu usage on the sender
packets.
Note that reducing number of wakes up increases cpu efficiency
decrease QPS
column2: as applications wont have the chance to warmup cpu caches

column1: doing a partial read of RPC requests/answers if they fit in one skb.
